messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: P1 - model-serving eu-west-1 high OOM rate (model-worker pods). Pager routed to primary. Link: https://incidents.internal/1761239876
Anya Patel: ugh im in the middle of a dentist appt, running late ~30m. paging secondary now — @Sam Ortega can you pick this up? :disappointed_relieved:
Sam Ortega: on it. stepping in as primary. first check — what's the immediate customer impact?
Anya Patel: brief summary from alerting: ~0.8% 503s across EU for the last 8m, 2 customers reported errors. runbook: https://runbooks.internal/model-oom-eu (see "fast mitigation")
oncall-bot: alert stream snippet: 
```
kubelet: OOMKill pid=14321 container=model-worker-3 memory=42.7Gi limit=48Gi at 2026-02-14T12:03:21Z
model-worker-3 logs: memory spike on batch inference; ctx: nightly-batch
```
Li Chen: quick pointer — if warm-pool is empty, route live traffic to the smaller quantized variant (quant-2). routing API accepts fallback param. we did that before for similar spikes.
Sam Ortega: checking warm-pool sizes... `curl -s https://infra.api/pool/eu-warm | jq .count` shows 0/6 healthy. that's bad.
Marta Svensson: I can run scale script from EU office. i can't take full primary (kids' nap), but can be secondary and execute ops.
Sam Ortega: please run: 
```
# scale model-worker eu
kubectl -n model scale deploy/model-worker-eu --replicas=4
# pause nightly batch
kubectl -n jobs annotate cronjob/nightly-batch paused=true --overwrite=true
```
Marta Svensson: running those now, will post results.
Marta Svensson: scale -> OK, new replicas scheduling. pause -> annotated. backup job status: SUSPENDED.
Sam Ortega: thanks. re-checking traffic: 503s drop to 0.2% over last 3m, but a couple of pods still show high RSS in logs.
Li Chen: if pods still OOM, we should fallback traffic to quant-2 while we drain bad pods. routing example: 
```
curl -X POST 'https://routing.redwood/v1/fallback' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE' -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","fallback":"quant-2","reason":"oom-spike-1761239876"}'
```
Sam Ortega: applied fallback. starting a rolling restart on model-worker-eu to evict bad nodes.
Sam Ortega: also creating incident bridge and tagging customers. @Marta can you join bridge if impact creeps back to >1%?
Marta Svensson: yep i'll join if that hits. bridge: https://meet.internal/bridge/1761239876
Anya Patel: FYI — if fallback doesn't hold, there's a hotfix branch that reduces per-batch memory; build id: hotfix/membound-20260214. deploy-bot can push a canary to 1 replica.
Sam Ortega: can we avoid deploy for now? risk is higher. prefer routing and scale first.
Li Chen: agrees. also adjusting kv-cache TTL to reduce repeated recompute: setting ttl=45s -> less mem pressure.
Sam Ortega: did TTL change, cache hit ratio improving. traffic stable at ~0.1% errors.
oncall-bot: customer-impact summary attached to incident: 2 customers affected intermittently, no major data loss, degraded latency for a subset of requests.
Sam Ortega: handoff plan — i'll stay primary until 16:00 UTC, Marta will be secondary and can take over if needed. Anya will take back as primary when back online. updating on-call rota.
Marta Svensson: noted. leaving logs/commands in thread for next person. will monitor next 45m then hand back to Sam if all clear.
Anya Patel: thanks team, sorry for the short notice. will confirm when i'm back and take a formal debrief later. please add any followups to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
Sam Ortega: closing loop — runbook steps executed: scaled to 4, paused batch, applied routing fallback, cache TTL adjusted. will capture timeline in the incident doc and add finger-of-root cause notes.
Marta Svensson: adding a quick note: scheduled a follow-up blameless postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Sam Ortega: last_message: monitoring continues, will escalate if error % >1% again. going to breathe. :sweat_smile:
